title: Windows support: ID lock and release archive
lead: Give adj an ID lock on Windows (LockFileEx), run the test suite on Windows in CI, and publish Windows release archives.
findings_note: AGENTS.md Store and config (lock_other.go: no lock, bounded retry only); release.yml builds no windows archive
boundary: **Not in this slice:** new dependencies (golang.org/x/sys is not allowed: use the standard library syscall package); changing lock behaviour on unix; installers, package managers or code signing; slicer catalog records (S20 runs in parallel and would take the same catalog id: record C32 decisions as slicer notes on S36; the outer session files them and the owner decisions at landing).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Owner decisions 2026-10-18: (1) the Windows lock is kernel32 LockFileEx called through the standard library (syscall.NewLazyDLL / NewProc), exclusive, on the same <store>/.adj.lock file, with flock's semantics: held from the ID scan to the link of the new file, released on return or process death, never deleted, the same 5 s wait polling every 10 ms (LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY in a loop) and the same error naming .adj.lock. (2) CI runs go test on windows-latest; tests that depend on unix permission bits are skipped on Windows with a reason. (3) release.yml adds windows amd64 and arm64 .zip archives holding adj.exe, listed in SHA256SUMS. Today lock_other.go has no lock on Windows (C114) and release.yml builds six tar.gz archives (C193).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- internal/store/lock_windows.go (new, //go:build windows): acquire via LockFileEx/UnlockFileEx.
- internal/store/lock_other.go: build tag narrowed so it no longer covers windows (still the fallback for other systems without flock).
- internal/store/lock_test.go and other tests: make the lock tests run on Windows where they are portable; skip (t.Skip with a reason, runtime.GOOS == "windows") only tests that assert unix permission bits or flock-specific errors (EACCES read-only fallback, ENOLCK). Keep the skips few and named.
- Any test or code with a path separator or line-ending assumption that breaks on Windows (filepath, not path; \n handling) found by GOOS=windows vet/compile and by reading.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: a windows-latest job running go vet ./... and go test ./... (no scripts/env.sh; plain go, as the macOS job does).
- .github/workflows/release.yml: windows amd64/arm64 builds of adj.exe, zipped (adj_<version>_windows_<arch>.zip), included in SHA256SUMS and the gh release upload.
- README.md (install: Windows zip), PROJECT.md (lock on Windows; Later: drop the Windows line), AGENTS.md (Store and config lock paragraph; release.yml description: eight archives), CHANGELOG.md (## Unreleased).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
Red first where the host allows; this host is darwin, so Windows tests can only be compiled here:
- internal/store/lock_windows_test.go (//go:build windows): a second acquire on the same file waits and then fails with the error naming .adj.lock after the timeout (use a short timeout), and succeeds after the first unlock; the lock file is never deleted.
- GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./... and GOOS=windows go test -c for each package with tests must succeed on darwin (this is the local red/green for the build tags: before the change lock_other.go is used on windows, so the new windows test must fail to find its behaviour; show it fails to compile or asserts no-lock today).
- The existing unix lock tests still pass on darwin unchanged.
Windows runtime results come only from CI after the owner pushes; the report must say so.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. lock_windows.go with LockFileEx (LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK | LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY, an OVERLAPPED struct, whole-file range) polled every 10 ms up to the timeout; UnlockFileEx and Close in unlock. Open the file with os.OpenFile(O_CREATE|O_RDWR) and use its Fd(); mirror lock_unix.go's structure and error messages.
2. Narrow lock_other.go's build tag; GOOS=windows vet must pass.
3. Audit tests for Windows: compile them for windows, read the ones touching permissions and paths, add skips with reasons only where the behaviour is unix-only.
4. CI job and release archives as in Files; keep the workflows standard library and shell only (no new actions beyond actions/checkout and actions/setup-go already used).
5. Docs. Record C32 decisions (e.g. which tests are skipped and why) as slicer notes on S36.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- . scripts/env.sh; go test ./...; go vet ./...; gofmt -l cmd internal prints nothing.
- GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go vet ./...; GOOS=windows GOARCH=arm64 go build ./cmd/adj; GOOS=windows go test -c -o <tmp> for each package with tests.
- Workflow YAML is valid (parse it with a stdlib-only check or read it carefully); release.yml's archive loop produces eight archives (dry-read).
- .cache/bin/adj lint --root . is clean.
- Mutation check each new test that runs on darwin; for windows-only tests, state that they could not run locally.
- slicer check --json is clean.
